Well, it's that time of year again. The wheat I planted last October is greening up nice, and I'm looking at the calendar thinking about cotton planting in a few weeks, then the mad rush when wheat comes off and maize goes in. I've got 40 mu total — that's a fair bit of land for just me and my wife at home now. The kids are off working in the city, so it's the two of us managing everything, which means I have to hire labor for the busy times, especially cotton picking.

Let me walk through what I'm thinking for each crop.

**Wheat (30 mu):** I planted 30 mu of wheat last fall, same as always. The stand looks decent this year — not amazing, but decent. I've already given it one irrigation at green-up in March when it was dry, and now it's jointing stage, so I'm putting on the topdressing. The extension fellow at the meeting last winter said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've been doing this for 30 years and I know my land. I put down compound fertilizer at planting — about 50 kg per mu — and now I'm spreading another 15 kg of urea per mu at jointing. That brings me to about 17 kg of pure N per mu total. A bit more than they recommend, but I'd rather waste a little money on extra fertilizer than risk a bad yield. Wheat is my safe crop. I'll irrigate again at heading if it doesn't rain, probably once more in May. That makes three irrigations total for the season. I'm hoping for about 420 kg per mu if the weather holds. I've sprayed herbicide already, and I'll watch for disease — if powdery mildew shows up, I'll spray fungicide, but otherwise I try to keep chemical costs down.

**Summer maize (30 mu, same fields after wheat):** Come mid-June, the custom combine harvests my wheat and I've got maybe a week to get the maize in the ground. There's no time for fancy tillage — I usually do minimal tillage or no-till and plant right behind the combine. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. It costs more than saving seed, but the yield difference pays for itself. For fertilizer, I spread compound at planting, about 45 kg per mu, and then topdress with urea at the jointing stage — maybe 15 kg per mu. That's roughly 15 kg of N per mu total. Maize in summer gets some rain, but I usually need to irrigate twice — once at jointing and once at filling if it's dry. Two times. I expect around 480 kg per mu. I'll spray herbicide at planting and keep an eye on armyworm.

**Cotton (10 mu):** I keep 10 mu in cotton even though it's a headache for labor. The price has been decent lately, and it diversifies my income. I plant in late April once the soil warms up. I use an improved cotton variety — not the most expensive hybrid, but a good reliable one my neighbor has had success with. For fertilizer, I go lighter on cotton than on grain: about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress with urea at flowering — around 15 kg per mu. Total N around 12 kg per mu. Cotton needs more pesticide — bollworm is always a threat — so I budget for insecticide and a bit of herbicide. I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll-setting. The big cost is picking. My wife and I can manage the planting, spraying, and irrigating, but picking is too much for just us. I hire pickers every autumn — paid by the jin picked. It costs me, but cotton brings in cash that wheat and maize don't always match. I'm hoping for about 260 kg per mu of seed cotton.

**Labor and money:** With just two of us, hired labor is my biggest headache after fertilizer costs. I need custom operators for wheat harvest and maize planting, and pickers for cotton. I'm watching my cash — I can't afford to go overboard on inputs even if the "optimal" rate is higher. I apply a bit more fertilizer than recommended because I'm loss-averse, but I don't buy the most expensive seeds or the newest chemicals. I stick with what I know works.
